description: A browser-based two-body orbit profile editor for Earth, Moon, and Mars. Users set periapsis and apoapsis altitude, select presets, control simulated time, and inspect the planar spacecraft state and classical orbital elements.

tests: Circular Earth orbit: eccentricity within 1e-15, radius within 1e-9 km, speed within 1e-12 km/s of vis-viva, period within 1e-9 s of the independent period expression, energy within 1e-11 km²/s² of −v²/2; LEO period also bounded to 5,500–5,600 s.

Earth 250 × 35,786 km altitude ellipse: periapsis radius within 1e-8 km, apoapsis within 1e-7 km, vis-viva speeds within 1e-11 km/s, radial velocity within 1e-12 km/s at each apsis, eccentricity within 1e-14.
Mars 300 × 100,000 km altitude orbit: position after one period closes within 1e-7 km per axis and velocity within 1e-10 km/s per axis.
Kepler solver at e = 0.98 and M = 2.4 rad: equation residual within 1e-12 rad.
Kepler solver at the maximum lunar UI altitude pair (100 × 200,000 km; e ≈ 0.98194865) and seven mean anomalies from 1e-6 to 6.2 rad: each residual within 1e-12 rad.
Earth transfer orbit at four elapsed-time samples: specific angular momentum invariant within 2e-8 km²/s and specific orbital energy within 2e-11 km²/s².
Body ordering and guardrails: unknown body, apoapsis below periapsis, and eccentricity 1 are rejected.

numericalAssumptions: Classical Newtonian, elliptic, two-body motion with a single central point mass and constant gravitational parameter.
The spacecraft is massless for propagation; spacecraft mass does not affect the orbit.
The orbital plane is fixed and represented in perifocal coordinates; no inclination, longitude of ascending node, or argument of periapsis is modeled.
Body radii are spherical reference radii: Earth 6,378.137 km, Moon 1,737.4 km, Mars 3,389.5 km. Altitude is measured above the selected reference radius.
Gravitational parameters in km³/s²: Earth 398,600.4418, Moon 4,902.800066, Mars 42,828.375214.
UI altitude controls keep periapsis at or above 100 km and apoapsis no lower than periapsis; the mechanics module also accepts non-negative periapsis altitude.
Canvas geometry is schematic and adaptively scaled. Numerical telemetry is computed from the same two-body orbit state.
limitations: No atmosphere or drag, oblateness/J2, third-body effects, thrust or maneuvers, body rotation, collision handling, or interplanetary transfer dynamics.
High-altitude configurations are still propagated as idealized bound two-body ellipses even where a real mission would need other bodies' gravity.
Canvas visuals, browser interactions, and performance were not browser-verified; the prompt disallowed localhost browser checks.
repairs: Changed the altitude note from “mean radius” to “reference radius” to accurately describe the selected body-radius convention.
